[`crate::graph::free_chain`]; this only writes.

entities.name: TOP_VALUES
entities.doc: The most frequent values one column keeps (perf/12 section 1).

entities.name: VALUE_CAP
entities.doc: Longest value a column statistic stores.

entities.name: column_stats
entities.doc:
The statistics of one column, over the order-preserving byte keys
of its values in row order.

entities.name: degree_cross
entities.signature: fn degree_cross(out: &[(u32, u32)], inn: &[(u32, u32)]) -> f64
entities.doc:
Sum over nodes of out-degree times in-degree, which is the number
of two hop paths the table holds. Both lists are sorted on their
first component, so the runs line up with a merge and a node
missing from either side contributes nothing.

entities.name: degree_histogram
entities.doc:
The log2 degree histogram of one direction, from an edge list
sorted by source: one run per source node, bucket `floor(log2 deg)`.

entities.name: degree_norms
entities.doc:
The lp norms of one direction's degree sequence, from the same
source-sorted edge list the histogram reads. The power sums run in
u128 because a hub-heavy graph can put the cube past what a u64
holds, and only the roots come back as f64.

entities.name: txn
entities.doc:
The single-writer commit path and its in-memory MVCC overlays.

Committed state per docs/08 section 2 is the base epoch data in the
file plus per-table overlays: appended rows, tombstones, property
update chains newest-first, and overlay edges, every entry stamped
with its commit epoch. A reader pinned at epoch E sees base data
plus overlay entries with commit epoch at or below E, so snapshots
stay consistent while the writer commits past them. Version data
never reaches the columnar file; a checkpoint folds overlays into
new sealed segments and recovery rebuilds them from the WAL alone.

Single writer is enforced by the borrow checker: [`Mvcc::begin`]
hands out a [`WriteTxn`] holding the store's only mutable borrow,
so a second writer cannot exist while one is open. Commit appends
the txn's records to the WAL, syncs through the `TxnCommit` frame,
and only then publishes the staged changes to the overlays, so a
crash on either side of the sync leaves the pre-txn or post-txn
state and nothing else.

entities.name: Cell
entities.doc:
One overlay cell value, the unit of an update chain entry and of an
appended row's column.

entities.name: Null
entities.doc:
The absence a `REMOVE` leaves behind. A column holds it the way
storage does, as a row whose validity bit is clear, so what the
fold writes for one of these is a bit rather than a value.

entities.name: IngestPayload
entities.doc:
The payload of one resolved or freshly written ingest: the sealed
data as the overlay will serve it until a fold seals it into the
base. The blocks in the file hold the durable copy; this is the
in-memory image recovery reads back from them.

entities.name: Mvcc
entities.doc:
The committed overlay store and the epoch counter, owned by
whichever handle owns the write side of the database.

entities.name: appended_rows
entities.signature: fn appended_rows(&self, table: u32, epoch: Epoch) -> u64
entities.doc: Rows appended to `table` and visible at `epoch`.

entities.name: appends_carry_columns
entities.signature: fn appends_carry_columns(&self, table: u32, epoch: Epoch) -> bool
entities.doc:
Whether any append batch of `table` visible at `epoch` carries
column values, which a fold must merge into stored props.

entities.name: begin
entities.doc:
Opens the write transaction. The mutable borrow is the writer
lock: a second call cannot compile while one txn is open.

entities.name: cell
entities.signature: fn cell(&self, table: u32, base_count: u64, offset: u64, col: u32, epoch: Epoch) -> Option<Cell>
entities.doc:
The newest overlay value of one cell at `epoch`: an update chain
entry first, then an appended row's stored column. `base_count`
is the row count of the sealed file, where appended offsets
start. Returns `None` when the base file holds the answer.

entities.name: edge_cells
entities.signature: fn edge_cells(&self, rel: u32, epoch: Epoch) -> impl Iterator
entities.doc:
The same edges with what they carry, which is what a fold of a
rel table that stores edge properties has to write.

entities.name: edges
entities.signature: fn edges(&self, rel: u32, epoch: Epoch) -> impl Iterator
entities.doc: Overlay edges of `rel` visible at `epoch`, for checkpoint folds.

entities.name: epoch
entities.doc: The newest committed epoch; a new reader pins this.

entities.name: has_updates
entities.signature: fn has_updates(&self, table: u32, epoch: Epoch) -> bool
entities.doc: Whether `table` holds any update chain entry visible at `epoch`.

entities.name: ingest_roots
entities.doc:
Manifest roots of ingests committed at or below `epoch`, for
the fold to free once their data is sealed into the base.

entities.name: is_deleted
entities.signature: fn is_deleted(&self, table: u32, offset: u64, epoch: Epoch) -> bool
entities.doc: Whether the row at `offset` is deleted for a reader at `epoch`.

entities.name: neighbors
entities.signature: fn neighbors(&self, rel: u32, node: u64, reversed: bool, epoch: Epoch, out: &mut Vec<u64>)
entities.doc:
Appends the overlay neighbors of `node` visible at `epoch` to
`out`: destinations of overlay edges leaving it, or sources of
edges entering it when `reversed`. Tombstoned endpoints are the
facade's concern; the overlay stores edges as committed.

entities.name: new
entities.doc:
A store with no overlays at the given committed epoch, the
state right after a checkpoint or a fresh create.

entities.name: recover
entities.doc:
Rebuilds the overlay store from the log: every committed txn
above `floor` replays into overlays exactly as its commit
published it, and the epoch counter resumes past the last one.
An `IngestRef` in the log is an error here; recovery with a
database file at hand goes through [`Self::recover_with`], whose
resolver reads the referenced sealed segments back.

entities.name: recover_with
entities.signature: fn recover_with(wal: &Wal, floor: Epoch, resolve: impl FnMut) -> Result<Self>
entities.doc:
[`Self::recover`] with a resolver that turns each committed
`IngestRef` back into its payload by reading the sealed
segments its manifest names, returning the payload and the
manifest root for the next fold to free.

entities.name: rels_touched
entities.doc: Rel tables holding overlay edges, sorted like the node tables.

entities.name: seed_tombstones
entities.signature: fn seed_tombstones(&mut self, table: u32, offsets: &[u64])
entities.doc:
Seeds tombstones a checkpoint persisted into the base file. They
enter at epoch 0 so every reader sees them, matching their state
as folded rather than freshly deleted.

entities.name: tables_touched
entities.doc:
Node tables holding any overlay state, sorted so a fold walks
them deterministically.

entities.name: tombstones

entities.doc: Tombstoned offsets of `table` visible at `epoch`, ascending.

entities.name: WriteTxn
entities.doc:
An open write transaction: stages mutations locally and publishes
them on [`WriteTxn::commit`]. Dropping it without committing
abandons everything staged, on disk and in memory alike.

entities.name: commit
entities.doc:
Commits: appends every staged record and the `TxnCommit` frame,
syncs, then publishes the overlays. The fdatasync inside
[`Wal::commit`] is the commit point; failure before it leaves
the store untouched and the tail torn, which replay drops.

entities.name: delete
entities.signature: fn delete(&mut self, table: u32, offset: u64)
entities.doc: Stages one row deletion.

entities.name: insert_nodes
entities.signature: fn insert_nodes(&mut self, table: u32, cols: Vec<(u32, Vec<Cell>)>) -> Result<u64>
entities.doc:
Stages a columnar batch of new rows for `table`. Every column
must carry the same row count.

entities.name: insert_rel
entities.signature: fn insert_rel(&mut self, rel: u32, src: u64, dst: u64)
entities.doc:
Stages one new edge carrying nothing, which is every edge in a
table that stores no properties on its edges.

entities.name: insert_rel_carrying
entities.signature: fn insert_rel_carrying(&mut self, rel: u32, src: u64, dst: u64, cols: Vec<(u32, Cell)>)
entities.doc:
Stages one new edge and the cells it holds: a column's position
in the rel table's props directory and the value this edge takes
there, one entry per column the table stores.

entities.name: is_empty
entities.doc: Whether nothing has been staged.

entities.name: update
entities.signature: fn update(&mut self, table: u32, offset: u64, col: u32, value: Cell)
entities.doc: Stages one cell update.

entities.name: verify
entities.doc:
Walks the whole file checking every crc: file header, database
headers, the catalog, the table index, and each rel table's group
directory with every column segment it lists, the primary-key index
included when the table carries one. Cross-checks the three
against each other (every rel table has a directory, every index
entry belongs to a catalog table, node entries decode as props
directories with row-aligned columns, counts agree), then decodes
the free list and
rejects a file whose free list claims a block a live chain or segment
uses, since allocating such a block would overwrite live data.
Returns the number of payload bytes verified.

entities.name: vfs
entities.doc:
The file shim under the storage layer.

[`Zu1File`](crate::file::Zu1File) and [`Wal`](crate::wal::Wal) do
their I/O through [`VfsFile`], whose methods are exactly the
syscalls the engine issues: positioned reads and writes, length
changes, and the two sync flavors. Production code runs on
[`RealFile`], a thin pass-through. The crash harness runs on
[`RecordingFile`], which logs every mutating call before forwarding
it, so a test can cut the log at any syscall boundary, rebuild the
file image a crash at that point could leave, and check recovery
against it. Reads are not logged; a crash cannot lose a read.

entities.name: IoEvent
entities.doc: One mutating syscall, in issue order across both files.

entities.name: Write
entities.signature: Write { file: IoFile, offset: u64, bytes: Vec<u8> }

entities.name: IoFile
entities.doc:
Which file an [`IoEvent`] belongs to. Sync barriers are per file:
syncing the database never makes an unsynced WAL write durable.

entities.name: IoLog
entities.doc: The shared log a workload's recording files append to.

entities.name: RealFile
entities.doc: The production implementation: every call is the syscall it names.

entities.name: create_new
entities.doc: Creates the file, failing when it already exists.

entities.name: open_or_create
entities.doc:
Opens for reading and writing, creating when missing, the WAL
contract.

entities.name: open_r
entities.doc:
Opens an existing file for reading only, so the operating
system refuses a write this process should not have attempted
and a database on a read-only mount opens at all.

entities.name: open_rw
entities.doc: Opens an existing file for reading and writing.

entities.name: RecordingFile
entities.doc: A pass-through that logs every mutating syscall before issuing it.

entities.signature: fn new(inner: RealFile, id: IoFile, log: IoLog) -> Self

entities.doc:
The syscall surface of one open file. `len` is fstat, hence the
`Result`; emptiness is the caller's question to ask of the value.

entities.signature: fn read_exact_at(&mut self, buf: &mut [u8], offset: u64) -> Result<()>

entities.name: set_len

entities.signature: fn write_all_at(&mut self, buf: &[u8], offset: u64) -> Result<()>

entities.name: wal
entities.doc:
Redo-only write-ahead log, the sidecar file next to a zu1 database.

The record format is the engine-shared one from docs/08 section 3:
`len: u32 LE | crc32c: u32 LE | body`, where the body is
`epoch: u64 LE | kind: u8 | payload` and both length and crc cover
the body. The s3 engine batches the same records into objects when
M5 lands; the sqlite engine delegates to SQLite's own WAL and never
touches this file.

Replay stops at the first frame that does not verify: a short
prefix, a length past the end of the file, or a crc mismatch all
mean the same thing, a torn tail from a crash mid-append, and
everything before the tear is intact because the single writer
appends frames in order. A frame whose crc verifies but whose
payload does not parse is different: that is corruption or version
skew, not a tear, and it surfaces as an error instead of a silent
stop. Delivery is transactional: records buffer per txn and reach
the sink only once their `TxnCommit` frame has been read, so a tear
after the last commit loses nothing that was promised durable.

entities.name: Wal
entities.doc:
The open sidecar log: an append position and the frame codec around
it. Commit durability is one `fdatasync` per commit; the 1 ms
group-commit window from docs/08 arrives with the writer queue.

entities.name: append
entities.signature: fn append(&mut self, epoch: Epoch, rec: &WalRecord) -> Result<()>
entities.doc:
Appends one frame without syncing. Durability comes from
[`Wal::commit`]; a crash before it tears the tail and replay
drops the whole uncommitted txn.

entities.name: commit
entities.signature: fn commit(&mut self, epoch: Epoch) -> Result<()>
entities.doc:
Appends the txn's `TxnCommit` frame and syncs the file. The
record hitting disk is the commit point: replay delivers a txn
exactly when this frame verifies.

entities.name: len
entities.doc: Bytes of intact frames, the input to the checkpoint trigger.

entities.name: open
entities.doc:
Opens the log at `path`, creating it when missing, and truncates
the torn tail so the next append starts at the last intact
frame. Crashing mid-append leaves a frame that fails its length
or crc check; everything before it is kept.

entities.name: open_on
entities.signature: fn open_on(file: Box<dyn VfsFile>, path: &Path) -> Result<Self>
entities.doc:
[`Self::open`] on an explicit file handle; the crash harness
passes a recording one.

entities.name: replay
entities.signature: fn replay(&self, floor: Epoch, sink: impl FnMut) -> Result<()>
entities.doc:
Replays committed transactions in log order through `sink`,
which sees every frame of a txn including its `TxnBegin` and
`TxnCommit`. Records with epoch at or below `floor` are already
folded into the base file and skip. A `CheckpointNote` raises
the floor the same way and is not delivered; the notes are
gathered in a first pass so a note folds the txns before it in
the log, which is where the txns it folded sit. Reads go
through a second descriptor so an open writer keeps its append
position.

entities.name: truncate
entities.doc:
Empties the log after a checkpoint has folded and published
everything it held.

entities.name: WalColumn
entities.doc:
One logged column of a node insert: the column's position in the
table's props directory and its row-ordered values.

entities.name: WalRecord
entities.doc:
One logical redo record. The epoch travels in the frame header, not
here: every record of a txn carries that txn's commit epoch.

entities.name: RelInsert
entities.signature: RelInsert { rel: u32, src: Vec<u64>, dst: Vec<u64>, cols: Vec<WalColumn> }

entities.name: Update
entities.signature: Update { table: u32, group: u64, col: u32, offsets: Vec<u64>, values: WalValues }

entities.name: WalValues
entities.doc:
Row-ordered values for one logged column, mirroring the two
property types the props store holds.

entities.name: Null
entities.doc:
This many absences in a row, which is what a `REMOVE` writes.
An absence carries nothing per row, so the count is the whole
record: what a reader needs to know is which rows the record
names, and the offsets beside it already say.
